messages:
alex: Hi! I'm a new eng, trying to get started with the Hosted API. Where do I find my sandbox API key in the console? Also, what are the sandbox quotas/rate limits so I don't accidentally hit them during load testing?

maria (devex): Welcome 👋 You should see your sandbox key in Console > Profile > API keys (top-right avatar menu). We issue a per-account sandbox key on signup. For quick local testing you can: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...` then `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'`

sam (eng): FWIW sandbox defaults: 60 req/min and a soft token quota of 100k tokens/day for new accounts. Rate limits are soft for dev accounts — you'll get 429s if you exceed. The API also returns rate headers (`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`) to help throttle.

rita (security): Quick note: do NOT send real customer PII or production data to the sandbox. Treat it as non-certified; for anything sensitive request a Private deployment or use a dedicated/sandbox with data controls.

alex: Thanks — should I create the key in the UI or is there an API to create one programmatically? Also, CI usage: is it safe to put the key in GitHub Actions secrets?

maria (devex): You can create/regenerate keys in the UI only (for now). For CI, yes use GitHub/GitLab secrets (do not commit keys). Use org-scoped keys for shared pipelines and rotate monthly. We recommend `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var naming convention.

ops-bot: Heads up: sandbox keys are ephemeral and will auto-expire after 90 days of inactivity. Regenerate from Console > Profile > API keys.

sam (eng): If you need higher sandbox quotas for a spike (integration test run), open the internal request form: https://intranet.redwood/forms/request-quota and tag `@eng-ops`. For load tests we usually request a temporary increase and use a dedicated test key.

alex: Perfect — last q: where can I see my usage breakdown so I know how many tokens I've used?

maria (devex): Console > Billing & Usage shows token/day and per-endpoint breakdown. There's also a `GET /v1/account/usage` endpoint for programmatic checks (requires your API key). Sample: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/account/usage`

rita (security): Also make sure to enable the audit-log retention if you'll be sharing logs with SRE — that helps with any accidental data exposures. Ping me if you want a quick checklist.

alex: Awesome, thanks everyone! Saved the links and will set REDWOOD_API_KEY in my local .env and GitHub secrets.

maria (devex): Welcome again! If anything is missing ping `#devex` or DM me. :party-parrot:
